item.title: Kenya confirms its first Ebola death as outbreak spreads
item.description:
JOSPIN MWISHA / AFP via Getty Images Kenya has confirmed its first-ever Ebola case after a citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo returned to Nairobi and later died. Health Minister Aden Duale said the patient, who had been ill for about a month, arrived in Kenya via Uganda on Saturday and was taken to a hospital, where he was isolated and tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain. He died on Monday night. Authorities have identified 28 contacts, including relatives and health workers, while tracing 23 passengers and four crew members from the same flight. Those contacts are being monitored for signs of infection. The case marks the fourth country affected by the current outbreak, after the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda and France. item.title: America Hits a New Debt Record at $40 Trillion and Counting
item.description:
Before the COVID-19 pandemic, in 2020 , the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) did not include the $40 trillion mark in its gross national debt projections for the coming decade, forecasting a gross federal debt of $36 trillion in 2030. By 2022, the CBO expected the country to cross $40 trillion in 2030. A year later , that date had moved up to 2028, and by 2024 , it had moved to 2027. The most recent report, from February 2026, projected that we would end the current fiscal year at $39.4 trillion. We have now surpassed the $40 trillion mark. The last time the federal government had a budget surplus was in FY 2001. Since then, Congress and presidents have overseen deficit after deficit. The previous record holder for the most debt amassed was President Barack Obama, whose two terms saw a $13.2 trillion increase in the national debt, adjusted for inflation.
